previous_disclosures.section: Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates > Change in Accounting Estimate
previous_disclosures.summary: In February 2023, the company completed an assessment of the useful lives of its property, plant, and equipment, increasing the estimated useful life of server, storage, and network equipment from three years to four to five years, and assembly and test equipment from five years to seven years. This change became effective at the beginning of fiscal year 2024 and is estimated to increase fiscal year 2024 operating income by $133 million due to reduced depreciation expense.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company reviews PP&E for impairment when carrying values may not be recoverable, recognizing losses if undiscounted cash flows are less than carrying value based on assumptions about future use and prices.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and MU disclose their approach to assessing the useful lives and impairment of Property, Plant, and Equipment (PP&E), specifically linking these assessments to technology transitions. NVDA explicitly states it increased useful lives for server, storage, and network equipment from three to four-to-five years and assembly equipment to seven years based on technological advances, resulting in a $135 million increase in operating income. MU discloses that it periodically assesses useful lives based on technology node transitions and reviews carrying values for impairment when indicators exist, though it does not report a specific quantified benefit from a change in estimate in the same manner as NVDA for this period.

sentences.text: Based on advances in technology and usage rate, we increased the estimated useful life of a majority of the server, storage, and network equipment from three years to a range of four to five years, and assembly and test equipment from five years to seven years.

The estimated effect of this change for fiscal year 2024 was a benefit of $33 million and $102 million for cost of revenue and operating expenses, respectively, which resulted in an increase in operating income of $135 million and net income of $114 million after tax, or $0.05 per both basic and diluted share.

Property, plant, and equipment: We periodically assess the estimated useful lives of our property, plant, and equipment based on technology node transitions, capital spending, and equipment re-use rates.

We also review the carrying value of property, plant, and equipment for impairment when events and circumstances indicate that the carrying value of an asset or group of assets may not be recoverable from the estimated future cash flows expected to result from its use and/or disposition.
